name: {perp} above {threshold} at {time}?
description: If the {perp} price at time of settlement is above {threshold} at {time}, Yes tokens pay out $1 each. Otherwise, No tokens pay out $1 each. Settlement is according to the {seconds}-second TWAP of {priceDescription} price before settlement time.

name: {competition} {stage}: {participantA} v {participantB}
description: This {sport} market has three possible results: {participantA}, Draw, or {participantB}. Exactly one corresponding named outcome resolves to Yes; the other two and the protocol-created fallback resolve to No. It covers the {contestType} between {participantA} and {participantB} in the {season} {competition} {stage}, scheduled for {scheduledStart} UTC (the "Contest"). The Contest Result is the official final result published by {officialSource}, including every period and tiebreak procedure that {officialSource} treats as part of the Contest. {participantA} resolves to Yes if the Contest Result names {participantA} the winner; {participantB} resolves to Yes if it names {participantB} the winner; Draw resolves to Yes if it records a draw, tie, or co-winners. If the Contest is postponed, delayed, or suspended, the Contest Result as ultimately completed applies if published by {resolutionDeadline} UTC. If {officialSource} names a listed participant the winner without a completed Contest after abandonment, walkover, forfeit, disqualification, retirement, withdrawal, or an administrative decision, that participant resolves to Yes. If no named outcome otherwise applies, Draw resolves to Yes if {officialSource} records a no contest or no winner, names anyone other than the listed participants the winner, the Contest is canceled without a replacement, or no Contest Result is published by {resolutionDeadline} UTC.  {officialSource} is the primary resolution source; independent reputable reporting may be used if it has not published the result. Once resolved, later appeals, corrections, reversals, or result reassignments do not change the resolution. This market is not endorsed by or affiliated with {officialSource}; names and marks are descriptive only. metadata=category:sports|subCategory:{sport}

name: {participant}
description: This outcome resolves to Yes if {participant} is the winner under the Contest Result or administrative-decision provisions of the parent question.

name: Draw
description: This outcome resolves to Yes if the Contest Result is a draw or tie or names co-winners, or if the official source records no contest or no winner, names an unlisted winner, cancels the Contest without a replacement, or does not publish a result by the deadline defined in the parent question.

name: {period} {award} winner
description: This {field} market covers the {period} {award} (the "Award"). Among editions of one award that {awardingBody} confers or administers with a winner due by {resolutionDeadline}, {period} identifies one by {awardingBody}'s labeling or, failing that, by the year its winner is due; otherwise the Award Result is unestablished. It has one named outcome per listed candidate plus one called Other, which may be registered at any time. Exactly one outcome resolves to Yes; all others resolve to No. An entry is one nominee, finalist, or winner of the Award as official channels record it, including a group recorded as one, with every work and person named on it as its nominee or recipient, even jointly, not as a member or representative of a group. A candidate identifies an entry if its Subject unambiguously identifies a work, group, or named person on that entry and no other entry of the Award. Official channels are the publications, events, and broadcasts of {awardingBody} and the Award's conferring body and administrator. The trigger is the earliest verifiable announcement on an official channel of the result: a winner, winners, or that the Award is withheld or not conferred; an announcement is not a trigger if, within one hour after it and before {resolutionDeadline}, it is withdrawn or removed or an official channel contradicts it. Fixing is the earlier of one hour after the trigger and {resolutionDeadline}, or {resolutionDeadline} without a trigger. The Award Result is the winner official channels have named as of fixing; a verifiably later statement supersedes earlier ones on the same channel or made at an event or broadcast, an explicit correction by fixing prevails across channels, other conflicts leave it unestablished, and omission is not a conflict. A candidate registered after the earliest official-channel announcement of a winner of the Award, whether or not it is a trigger, or that identifies no entry at fixing, resolves to No. A candidate finally resolves to No once official channels publish final nominees or finalists none of which it identifies or show it identifies the same entry as an earlier registered candidate. Of the remaining candidates, the earliest registered identifying the one winning entry the Award Result names resolves to Yes; all others resolve to No. Other resolves to Yes if no candidate resolves to Yes, including if the Award Result is unestablished at fixing, names no winner, or names more than one winning entry, such as a tie. Only evidence public by 24 hours after fixing establishes the trigger and the Award Result at fixing; timestamps must prove when contents were public; a Yes resolution occurs only after that cutoff. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any entity referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:culture|subCategory:{field}|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to the single winner of an award or honor, not a selection for office or candidacy.

name: {candidate}
description: This outcome resolves to Yes if, under the parent question's rules, it is the earliest registered candidate not otherwise resolved to No that identifies the one winning entry of the Award, and otherwise resolves to No. Its Subject is {subject}. A Subject that identifies a work, group, or named person on more than one entry, or that {candidate} does not name in full or in short form, identifies no entry. Resolution follows the parent question's timing and source rules. {candidate} is a display label.

name: {company} IPO confirmed by {dateTime}
description: The market resolves to Yes if {company}'s first public common-equity offering for a regulated exchange listing is publicly confirmed at or before {dateTime}. Otherwise, it resolves to No. Confirmation occurs when any of these becomes public: a securities regulator approves or clears the required filing for the public offering; the company or underwriters publish final share count and offering price; or the exchange assigns a ticker and grants unconditional listing approval. Conditional exchange approval qualifies only when the exchange publicly confirms all conditions satisfied. These triggers are independent. All triggers require a qualifying offering. Filing or confidential submission, a proposed price range, ticker reservation, or intent alone do not qualify. Trading need not begin by the deadline. Issuer identity and offering structure are assessed when each trigger becomes public. Prior trading means trading before that trigger, excluding trading resulting from that offering. Later restructuring, delay, withdrawal, or cancellation does not undo qualifying confirmation; corrections may show it never qualified. Name changes of the same issuer count; offerings by a parent, subsidiary, or acquirer do not. Prior public common-equity trading on a regulated exchange disqualifies the company, even if later taken private. Prior trading outside a regulated exchange disqualifies it if retail investors could buy and sell its common equity without investor qualification requirements, invitation, or issuer approval. Routine account opening and identity checks do not restrict access. A direct listing providing for newly issued common shares to be sold to the public qualifies; a resale-only direct listing does not. SPAC transactions, reverse mergers, private placements, and offerings of debt, preferred shares, or depositary receipts without a common-equity IPO do not qualify. Evidence and corrections must be public by seven days after {dateTime}; resolution occurs only after that cutoff. They establish whether a qualifying confirmation was public by the deadline. Official source priority is regulator, company, exchange, then underwriters. Priority resolves contradictions about the same fact; silence does not negate another source's confirmation. Unresolved conflicts at the highest applicable priority leave a fact unestablished. Otherwise, at least two independent reputable news organizations' original reports may establish missing facts if reputable reporting has no unresolved material contradiction. Syndicated copies count as one. Reporting cannot override official facts or resolve official conflicts; rumors do not qualify. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any entity referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:economics|subCategory:N/A|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to confirmation of a company's initial public offering.

name: {participantA} v {participantB}: {shortNameA} {spread}
description: This {sport} market covers the contest between {participantA} ({shortNameA}) and {participantB} scheduled for {scheduledStart} (the "Contest"). Counted Play is {countedPlay}; extra time, overtime, shoot-outs, and tiebreaks count only if expressly included. The Final Value is {participantA}'s {measure} plus {spread} minus {participantB}'s {measure}, each {measure} taken over Counted Play only. {spread} is a + or - sign followed by a decimal in {measure}'s units and scale. Reported values use published precision. Derived measures are calculated from underlying statistics without rounding. Unclear units or calculations leave the Final Value unestablished. Completion requires all Counted Play to conclude. For full-contest scopes, normal endings under rules in force at scheduled start, including mercy rules and unneeded periods, count. Abandonment, retirement, weather-shortening, forfeits, and awarded results do not complete unfinished Counted Play. Postponement, suspension, rescheduling, or replay after incomplete Counted Play retains the participants and deadline; lineups may change. Resumed play continues the record; a full replay replaces it. An individual participates only by entering Counted Play. The market resolves to 0.5 if completion, the Final Value, or any individual participant's participation is unestablished at fixing. Otherwise, it resolves to Yes if the Final Value exceeds 0, to No if below, and to 0.5 if equal. Only evidence public by {resolutionDeadline} establishes trigger time and source contents at fixing; resolution occurs only after that deadline. The trigger is the earliest verifiable official publication time for a record establishing completion, final statistics, and whether each relevant individual participated; absent that, its earliest verifiable capture time. Timestamps must prove contents existed then. Fixing is the earlier of one hour after the trigger and {resolutionDeadline}, or that deadline without a trigger. {officialSource}'s record establishes the facts. A verifiably newer version supersedes older versions of that record. Across official channels, an explicit correction or designation of authority prevails; other conflicts leave facts unestablished. Only versions public by fixing determine facts. Only if fixing is on {resolutionDeadline} may at least two independent reputable news organizations' original reports establish missing facts, with no unresolved material contradiction in reputable reporting. Syndicated copies count as one. Reporting cannot override official facts or resolve official conflicts. Changes after fixing and evidence after the deadline do not affect resolution. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any entity referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:sports|subCategory:{sport}|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to a spread in a single scheduled sports contest.
